lesson: TWO RULES. A high-volume market pricing ONE BUCKET ABOVE our observed max is therefore evidence we are behind, not a mispricing to fade. lesson: Both six-hour groups read 84.92 and the 14:51 snapshot read 84.92, yet the true peak came at 3:19 PM. Three sources agreeing on a value is not evidence the max is in -- the day simply touched the same level twice, once before 2 PM and again at 3:19 PM, and the 0.5F settlement rounding hides the difference. SECOND CONSECUTIVE DAY THE PRELIMINARY CLI's TIMESTAMP WAS WRONG: it said 2:09 PM, the final says 3:19 PM (Aug 9: said 1:48 PM, final said 4:02 PM). Both times the preliminary placed the peak BEFORE 2 PM when it actually fell after. That is now a directional bias, not noise, and it is the worst possible direction for this project: it makes the 13:51 group look like it captured the day when it did not. Rule stands and hardens -- a preliminary CLI settles nothing, in value or in time. Seventh consecutive day the NYC peak fell at or after 2 PM (2:28, 5:32, 2:39, 1:51, 4:02, 3:19 -- with Aug 6's 12:29 PM the only genuine exception in the run).
